title: Comparison of derived local restriction with exact inverse image and slice restriction
statement:
Let $g:S\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $U$ an object of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Use the actual inverse-image ring $R'=g^{-1}R$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and its restriction $R'_U$ to the slice over $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Write $F_g:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R')$ for module inverse image without extension to a different coefficient ring, and $G_U:\operatorname{Mod}(R')\to\operatorname{Mod}(R'_U)$ for slice restriction. These are exact. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], choose the localization representative $C$ of $DF_g(K)$ and define $L_{g,U}(K)=Q_U(G_U C)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]. There is a comparison
$$DG_U(DF_gK)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{g,U}(K)$$
obtained from the localization representative isomorphism and the exact-functor localization factor [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], which also defines $DF_g$ and $DG_U$. It transports morphisms and isomorphisms of $K$ functorially and is compatible with the natural isomorphisms
$$G_UF_gH^q(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(L_{g,U}K),\qquad L_{g,U}(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(G_UF_gM)[r].$$
Here $q,r\in\mathbf Z$, $M$ is any $R$-module sheaf, and $M[r]$ is its degree-zero complex shifted by $r$. No immersion, flatness, boundedness, or equality between $g^{-1}R$ and another scheme's completed coefficient ring is assumed.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor: exact functors on unbounded derived categories), applied to actual inverse-image and localized module restriction; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.11(3), implicit local cohomology comparison. The representative normalization is the DAG ringed-site-derived-restriction convention.

proof.text: Put $F=F_g$ and $G=G_U$. On underlying abelian sheaves, $F$ is naturally isomorphic to the exact abelian inverse image: use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-inverse-image-comparison] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], with the base-change functor defining $g^{-1}$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The forgetful functors from modules are faithful and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. They reflect exact sequences: by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] the underlying homology of a sequence is the homology of its underlying sequence; a module with zero underlying abelian sheaf is zero, since faithfulness makes its identity zero. Applying this to the image under $F$ of a short exact sequence proves exactness of $F$. Additivity follows by forgetting addition of maps and using faithfulness. This uses the module action over the actual ring $g^{-1}R$, with no extension to a different ring.

On the ringed site $(S_{\mathrm{proet}},R')$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-restriction-exact] says that restriction of $R'$-module sheaves to $R'_U$-module sheaves on the slice over any object $U$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits; the site is small because the pro-etale site is taken on its chosen small skeleton, as in the statement's pro-etale site convention. A functor between abelian categories preserving finite limits and finite colimits is additive (Tag 010N (1)), so $G$ is exact as a functor of module sheaves, not merely of abelian sheaves. Its source and target rings and its sectionwise formula are precisely those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No assumption that $U$ is an open subscheme or immersion is introduced.

source.place: Section 03DH (section-localize), Definition 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site), localization morphism with identity structure map; homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor) (1).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] separately to $F$ and $G$. Write $C(F),C(G)$ for their termwise complex functors, $Q_T,Q_S,Q_U$ for localization, and write their natural factorization isomorphisms as $\varphi^F_A:DF(Q_TA)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_SC(F)A$ and $\varphi^G_B:DG(Q_SB)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_UC(G)B$. The factors commute with every integer shift. In particular no boundedness or resolution hypothesis is needed for either factor.

For $X=DF(K)$ let $C$ be the chosen localization representative in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction], with its representative isomorphism $\epsilon_X:Q_SC\xrightarrow{\sim}X$. By definition $L(K)=Q_UC(G)C$. Define, in functional order,
$$\alpha_K=\varphi^G_C\circ DG(\epsilon_X^{-1}):DG(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}L(K).$$
Both arrows are isomorphisms, so this proves the asserted comparison. For $a:K\to K'$ define
$$L(a)=\alpha_{K'}\circ DG(DF(a))\circ\alpha_K^{-1}.$$
Cancellation of $\alpha_K^{-1}\alpha_K$ proves $L(1)=1$ and $L(ba)=L(b)L(a)$. This also gives $L(a)\alpha_K=\alpha_{K'}DG(DF(a))$ and $L(a^{-1})=L(a)^{-1}$ whenever $a$ is invertible. Thus an objectwise choice of representative need not be a functor on complexes: these formulas supply the functor on derived objects.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); explicit conjugation using the localization representative convention.

proof.text:
The construction also compares with every other representative. If $b:Q_SB\xrightarrow{\sim}X$, set $\lambda_{B,b}=\varphi^G_B\circ DG(b^{-1})$. The comparison from the chosen local object to $Q_UC(G)B$ is $\lambda_{B,b}\alpha_K^{-1}$. Comparisons for three representatives compose because the middle $\lambda^{-1}\lambda$ cancels. If $h:B\to B'$ is a chain map and $t:X\to X'$ satisfies $t b=b'Q_S(h)$, naturality of $\varphi^G$ gives
$$Q_UC(G)(h)\lambda_{B,b}=\lambda_{B',b'}DG(t).$$
Indeed substitute $Q_S(h)b^{-1}=(b')^{-1}t$ in that naturality equation. The same equation holds after inverting quasi-isomorphisms, since $C(G)$ preserves them. The localization universal property therefore gives the corresponding equation for arbitrary derived morphisms. This identifies the transported functor with termwise restriction on any representative, including the maps.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); localization at quasi-isomorphisms, explicit factorization naturality calculation.

proof.text:
For an exact functor $E$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives natural isomorphisms $c^q_{E,A}:H^q(C(E)A)\xrightarrow{\sim}E H^q(A)$, induced by its maps on kernels and images. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], both sides factor through localization: the first through $DE$ and $\varphi^E$, and the second through $H^q$. Thus the inverse of $c^q$, composed with the inverse cohomology of $\varphi^E$, gives
$$h^q_{E,Y}:E H^q(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(DE(Y)).$$
This formula on $Y=QA$ extends to all derived objects and maps: naturality holds on chain maps by naturality of $c^q$ and $\varphi^E$, on inverses of quasi-isomorphisms by cancellation, and hence on localization morphisms. Apply it to $F$ and $G$. The required local comparison is explicitly
$$G F H^q(K)\xrightarrow{G(h^q_{F,K})}G H^q(DFK)\xrightarrow{h^q_{G,DFK}}H^q(DGDFK)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha_K)}H^q(LK).$$
Naturality of the first two arrows and the equation for $L(a)$ in step 4 prove naturality of this composite. Step 5 identifies it on any representative with the kernel/image comparison for termwise $GF$, so it is compatible with $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor), kernel and image comparison; derived.tex Tag 015F and the localization definition.

proof.text:
For $M[0]$, termwise application gives the degree-zero complexes $F(M)[0]$ and $GF(M)[0]$: an additive exact functor sends the zero object and zero differentials to zero. Factorization therefore gives $DF(M[0])\cong F(M)[0]$ and $DG(F(M)[0])\cong GF(M)[0]$. Combine these with the integer-shift isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to obtain
$$DGDF(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(GF M)[r].$$
Composing with $\alpha_{M[r]}^{-1}$ gives the asserted $L(M[r])\cong(GFM)[r]$. The shift/factorization compatibility in that cited statement makes this the comparison computed on $M[0][r]$: in degree $n$ the term is $GF(M[0]^{n+r})$ and the differential is $(-1)^rGF(d^{n+r})$, the same on both sides. The cohomology comparison of step 6 uses those same kernels and image projections. On this single complex it is the identity on $GFM$ in degree $-r$, and the unique map between zero objects in other degrees. Step 5 transports these equalities to the chosen representatives. Consequently the single/shift and cohomology comparisons agree with $\alpha$ and with maps of $M$, for positive, zero and negative $r$.
